also: at the top of one’s voice

terms.gloss: at most, at the utmost; at the latest
terms.grammar: adverb (neuter of summus), after the number or time it limits
evidence: Cic. Att. 13.21.2: hodiē aut summum crās
Traupman 102: hodiē, summum crās, today, at latest tomorrow
Traupman 212, 213: vīgintī aut summum trīgintā minūtīs, in twenty or at most thirty minutes
terms.comment: The everyday way to cap a number: “two or three times at most”; with a time, “at the latest”. Lewis & Short gives it under superus (summus).

terms.gloss: as much as possible, the most one can
terms.grammar: phrase: quam with the superlative plūrimum, as noun or adverb
evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.150: caput autem est … quam plūrimum scrībere
Cic. Rab. Post. 39: ut habēret quam plūrimum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Quam with any superlative gives “as … as possible”: quam celerrimē, quam maximus (see most).

terms.gloss: highest, utmost: the maximum (of speed, effort, volume)
evidence: Hor. S. 1.3.7: summā vōce, at the top of his voice (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The adjective for a maximum reached: summā vōce, at full volume. See extreme.

phrases.latin: ā tē vērō bis terve summum et eās perbrevīs accēpī
phrases.english: but from you I have had two or three letters at most, and very short ones

phrases.latin: exspectābam hodiē aut summum crās ab eō tabellāriōs
phrases.english: I was expecting couriers from him today, or tomorrow at the latest

phrases.latin: Caput autem est, quod, ut vērē dīcam, minimē facimus (est enim magnī labōris, quem plērīque fugimus), quam plūrimum scrībere.
phrases.english: But the main thing, which, to tell the truth, we do least (for it is hard work, which most of us avoid), is to write as much as possible.
Perhaps tomorrow, at the latest the day after.
